question: Viscera intended for forensic science laboratory (FSL) chemical analysis should be preserved in 10% formalin before dispatch.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Formalin must NEVER be used for viscera going to the FSL. Formalin is for histopathology specimens only. FSL specimens require saturated common salt solution (saline) to preserve them for chemical/toxicological analysis.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is FALSE. Formalin fixation destroys the chemical integrity of the specimen and renders it useless for toxicological analysis. FSL-destined viscera must be preserved in saturated saline (for chemical analysis) or normal saline; never formalin.
